text.text_excerpt: I have not stayed in the hotel but have been to the bar several times most recently a week ago. It is a great little place for live music and great drinks! The bar area itself is small but it extends into the side area with comfy seating and great art, and back to the courtyard which is lovely in the evening. The music is Old time New Orleans music and unlike you will hear most places. My husband always enjoys the music regardless of who is playing. The service is so friendly, you never mind when it is busy and you have to wait a bit. It is the flavor and personality of all that is New Orleans, so if you want that experience, this is the place to go! It also has an awesome happy hour ever...

This review is for the live music and small bar area attached to the hotel. This is a great venue for live music that is more removed from the hustle and bustle of the main Frenchman Street area. Both the MOJITO and the CAPHIRINHA were tart, well-made and treated wonderful. Javier, the bartender, is attentive and makes well balanced drinks. Lynn Drury was playing live music on a Tuesday night and she had a great selection of original songs. I do recommend not staying in room 101, which is literally right across from the men's restroom in a small alcove. The communal seating area is comfortable with a relaxed atmosphere. Looks like a relatively quiet, low key option in a busy and loud area...

Great location and nice cocktail bar. Some evenings are filled with live music in the lobby. I've listened to bands twice here- seems to take me back to another time. The strumming of an acoustic guitar and a strong pretty voice that bleeds into the streets. However, was quite noisy early in the morning. I guess housekeeping was cleaning upstairs and there was loud trampling of feet for about an hour. Otherwise, friendly staff and room was super clean. Simple, clean, & Pricy bc was overlooking the street/ park.
